verdict.left_looks: A tall red-and-white banded lighthouse tower on a stone plinth, with a dark grey stepped cap, a glazed lantern room with railings on top, and a small brown-roofed cottage beside it. The tower is clean and evenly coloured with flat stripes. The cottage has a plain grey wall, dark wooden roof, and a chimney. Materials are smooth and uniform, with little texture. The water and grass base are simple.
verdict.right_looks: A squatter lighthouse tower with the same red-and-white banding, set on a mossy cobble and stone base that steps out in layers. Stone surround windows are set into the tower. A glazed lantern with wooden framing and a dark roof sits on top. A low cottage at the base has a terracotta tiled roof, a stone chimney with a torch, timber posts, and a plastered wall. The cottage and base look weathered and mixed, with moss and cobble patches that read as deliberate patina, not damage. The tower leans slightly in some views.
verdict.why: The right build has a grounded stone base, window surrounds, and a richer, textured palette (moss, cobble, terracotta, timber) that make it read as a lived-in lighthouse with character, while the left is clean but flat and generic.
